title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous pages. This is a combinatorial, one-dimensional model inside Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' rewrite, a tame-topology or stratified-space programme.

- L is an ordered set of 'lieux' (points). Possibly it is totally ordered; 'Drap(L)' is used for finite totally ordered subsets, i.e. finite chains or 'flags'.
- M = M_0 ∪ M_1 is the set of 'multiplicités' (elementary strata): the points P_x (x ∈ L) and the open segments S_{a,b} (a < b).
- For a stratum X, δX is its set of end-lieux: δP_x = {x}, and δS_{a,b} = |∂S_{a,b}| = {a,b}.
- X ≍ Y ('mutually compatible') means, roughly, that X and Y can occur together as strata of one subdivision.
- The previous page proved a necessary condition: X ≍ Y ⇒ δX ∪ δY ∈ Drap(L).
- For a flag T = {t_1 < ... < t_n} it defined the interstitial segments S_{t_i,t_{i+1}} and the interstitial lieux P_{t_i}.

Proposition on this page. Let F ⊂ M be finite and non-empty, and set δF = ∪_{X∈F} δX. Then F consists of pairwise compatible multiplicities if and only if:
- (i) δF is a flag, δF ∈ Drap(L);
- (ii) every element of F is interstitial for δF. Concretely, each point of F is some P_t with t ∈ δF (automatic), and each segment of F joins two consecutive elements of δF.

The proof is announced 'by induction on card F' but not written.

Consequence. For a given non-empty flag T there is a largest family of mutually compatible strata with δF = T. It is F_T, the set of all interstitial strata of T, namely the points P_{t_i} and the segments S_{t_i,t_{i+1}}. Grothendieck calls F_T the 'figure canonique' defined by T. In modern terms, this is the cell decomposition of the polygonal interval [t_1, t_n] with vertex set T. The next page adds that T = δF_T, so T ↦ F_T is injective. It also introduces flags of flags (an order on non-empty flags) to treat compatibility of figures.

Start of the next topic. He considers the simplest non-trivial figure, F = \tilde S_{a,b} = {S_{a,b}, P_a, P_b}, a closed segment with its two endpoints. He looks at the three 'supports' 𝔖_a = supp° P_a, 𝔖_b = supp° P_b and 𝔖_{ab} = supp° S_{a,b}. These presumably live in an ambient stratified space whose strata are labelled by M. He announces a case analysis of the relative position of these three supports, two at a time, saying there are exactly three non-trivial cases. The page breaks off there.

The left margin note reads roughly 'lien entre multiplicités compatibles et partitions'. This hints at relating compatible families to partitions or subdivisions.

Purpose of the page: to give a combinatorial description of which elementary strata can coexist in one stratification of a 1-dimensional tame space. This is a building block for describing stratified spaces through their combinatorial 'figures'.
errors: Pairwise compatibility gives that δX ∪ δY is a chain for every pair X, Y in F. Any two elements of δF lie in some such δX ∪ δY, so they are comparable and δF is a chain; this step is fine.

The sufficiency direction, and whether (ii) is needed beyond pairwise checks, depends on the exact definition of ≍ (from earlier pages, not shown). The proof is only announced ('par récurrence sur card F'), so the claim is unproved on this page.

The deleted remark 'δF = ∅ ssi F = ∅' explains why the 'non vide' hypothesis was added. For card T = 1 the interstitial segment set is empty, which the previous page flagged as 'à vérifier'. This is consistent with F_{{t}} = {P_t} on the next page.

ideas.what: Characterisation of mutually compatible finite families of 0- and 1-dimensional strata on an ordered line: the boundary set is a flag and all members are interstitial.
ideas.modern_name: Cells of a common subdivision of an interval; faces of a 1-dimensional polyhedral (simplicial) complex on a chain
ideas.where_published: Unpublished Analysis situs notes (cote 156); not in Esquisse or Pursuing Stacks in this form

ideas.what: Canonical figure F_T attached to a flag T: the maximal compatible family with δF = T, with T recovered as δF_T.
ideas.modern_name: Cell decomposition / subdivided interval determined by its vertex set; maximal face poset of a stratification

ideas.what: Studying relative positions of the 'supports' supp° of the strata of a closed segment (two endpoints plus open segment) in an ambient space; case analysis into three non-trivial cases.
ideas.modern_name: Incidence/frontier conditions for strata of a stratified (tame) space; exit-path or poset-stratified combinatorics
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney/Thom/Mather (frontier condition); later exit-path ∞-categories (MacPherson, Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 sketches tame topology only programmatically

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins a classification of the relative positions of the supports of the strata of a closed segment ('trois cas exactement non triviaux'). He also notes a link between compatible multiplicities and partitions. The page stops before either is developed; the continuation would be in the following pages of the same notes.
missed.quote: La position des supports concerne une sous-relation de cet ensemble de trois éléments ... Il y a manifestement trois cas exactement non triviaux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. It documents Grothendieck's concrete combinatorial approach to tame stratified spaces, of interest to historians of 'topologie modérée'. The mathematics itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an elementary combinatorial lemma: compatible strata on a line correspond to interstitial cells of a flag. It also defines the 'canonical figure' and starts an unfinished case analysis. The material is routine and of historical interest only, as part of the unpublished Analysis situs drafts.
transcription_corrections: Condition (ii): 'indécomposables pour δF' should read 'interstitiels pour δF' (consistent with the previous page's definition of interstitial segments and lieux).
'ensemble des toutes les strates indécomposables de T' should read 'ensemble de toutes les strates interstitielles de T'.
The margin note appears to read 'lien entre multiplicités compatibles et partitions' (partly uncertain).
The page number in the header looks like '98' (written as '88'/'98'); the archive foliation at the bottom is 97.
